summary.short: Amends Mexico's CNBV general provisions for credit institutions to permit facial biometric identity verification alongside fingerprints, checked against official registries, and sets technical and security requirements for biometric databases (Annex 71). Applies from the day after DOF publication.
summary.long: CNBV resolution dated 25 June 2026 amending Articles 51 Bis, 51 Bis 2, 51 Bis 3, 51 Bis 4 and 51 Bis 5 of the general provisions for credit institutions and replacing Annex 71. Credit institutions must verify, for in-person operations, that the biometric data of the person presenting an identity document matches official registries, with a 90% match for fingerprints and an online check of facial biometrics added. Institutions may build their own biometric databases in place of certain requirements, subject to matching against official registries, notice to the Commission within 20 business days, annual validation of security mechanisms, and deletion of data when use stops. Biometric data may not be sold, transferred, shared or interoperated with other institutions or third parties for identity checks. The Commission may request information and, after a hearing, order partial or total suspension of a database for serious or repeated non-compliance. The Commission may also authorise alternative processes and documents. Annex 71 sets capture requirements and security controls such as segregation, encryption and penetration testing. Institutions must comply within 90 business days of entry into force, the day after DOF publication.

obligations.summary: Institutions must require persons who apply in person for passive operations linked to Level 4 accounts, or for active operations, services or payment means linked to Levels 3 and 4, to provide identity data and perform the verification actions of Art. 51 Bis 4 fracción I for the person presenting; no online biometric verification of a represented person.
